summary: Privacy-impact audit field-mapping and live query handoff for SIEM onboarding
description:
Issue summary:
Meridian Trust Bank is onboarding Redwood's audit stream into their SIEM and needs a privacy-impact oriented field mapping plus a live query handoff. They require a compact sample extract and a signed manifest that demonstrates PII redaction rules applied, plus an example live query (Splunk search / SumoLogic query equivalent) that their SOC can run to validate record lineage.

Impact:
Customer cannot complete SOC ingestion tests and legal review for go-live. This is blocking their scheduled compliance sign-off next week. They have paused downstream alerting tests until they receive the mapping and proof artifacts.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted audit export in prod (us-east primary, eu-west fallback)
- Delivery configured as hourly NDJSON batches to customer S3 (s3://meridian-trust-logs/redwood/audit)
- SIEM connector reference: seim-bridge v1.3.2 (deployed in their AWS account via CloudFormation)

Request details:
1) Produce a field-level mapping document (CSV and brief JSON schema) that annotates which audit fields are considered PII, which are pseudonymized, and which are safe. Include canonical examples and the canonical UTC timestamp format used.
2) Provide a signed sample export (hour slice with 100 events) with redaction applied and a corresponding manifest (SHA256 checksums) so their legal team can verify chain of custody.
3) Provide two short live-query examples (one Splunk SPL, one SumoLogic query) that demonstrate how to filter for a user-session across events and how to validate that the pseudonymization is deterministic across the slice.
4) Cross-reference the mapping to our retention and deletion policies, and call out any fields that require legal exception for retention >90 days.

Attachments requested in reply: sample_export.ndjson, mapping.csv, manifest.sig, live_query_examples.txt

Contact at customer: Priya Nair (pri.nair@meridiantrust.com) - SOC Manager
Redwood account: mtrust-enterprise-02
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer configured S3 delivery as per onboarding guide (hourly).
2) Customer attempted to validate sample using Splunk; they reported unexpected raw_email field present in sample and uncertain deterministic pseudonymization of user_id across events.
3) Customer opened support after legal requested signed manifest and PII field classification.

Reproduction notes for Support: use replica export job id audit-export-20260310-07 in prod us-east to generate a 1-hour slice; run our redaction pipeline with --test-mode to produce annotated sample and manifest.

- Export job audit-export-20260310-07 completed successfully, 12,340 events.
- Redaction worker w-redact-5 ran with no fatal errors; 0x03 warnings on email-normalization for 18 events.
- Delivery to customer S3 succeeded (200 OK).
- Sample manifest generation produced checksum file manifest-20260310-07.sha256.
- Customer Splunk ingest tests show raw_email present for ~18 events where normalization flagged domain-literals.
References: s3://redwood-exports/prod/audit-export-20260310-07/, link to logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/exports/2026/03/10/audit-export-07
requested_deliverables:
- mapping.csv (columns: source_field, description, pii_classification, pseudonymization_method, retention_days, example_value)
- signed_sample_ndjson (100 events) with redaction applied
- manifest.sig (SHA256 checksums, timestamped and signed with Redwood export KMS key)
- live_query_examples.txt (Splunk and SumoLogic versions)
- short note (1 page) mapping redaction rules to retention policy and legal exceptions
